line.name: CyB by Joya de Nicaragua
line.background_text: CyB (originally launched as "Cuenca y Blanco") was the first collaboration between Joya de Nicaragua and cigar maker Jose Blanco following his 2011 arrival at the company, after roughly a year of development. It marked a departure from JDN's tradition of all-Nicaraguan puros, blending tobaccos from four countries: Nicaragua, Dominican Republic, Ecuador and Peru. The line was renamed from "Cuenca y Blanco" to "CyB" in October 2012 to avoid a potential trademark conflict; the blend itself was unchanged. A Lancero Fino vitola (7 x 38) was later released in 2013 as a TAA exclusive.

vitolas.summary_review: Blind Man's Puff scored this highly across all five panelists, praising thick, creamy smoke and strong construction, with a flavor arc from red pepper/cedar to roasted coffee to cinnamon and cocoa/pecan.

critic_reviews.key_notes_text: Great (94/100); red pepper and cedar opening, roasted coffee midpoint, cinnamon/cocoa/pecan finish.

vitolas.summary_review: A 2013 TAA-exclusive vitola; halfwheel's initial (prerelease) review found inconsistency, but a later 2014 redux review found the blend had improved with age.

critic_reviews.key_notes_text: Original prerelease review; inconsistent construction noted.
Redux review; "a much better cigar than it was when it shipped."

research_notes: Corona Real, Lonsdale Club, and Toro Supremo/Torpedo Especial dimensions are confirmed via Blind Man's Puff's line overview but no individual reviews were found for these three vitolas, so tasting notes/scores are left empty. Overall blend composition confirmed via halfwheel's CyB reviews, not a single canonical spec sheet.
